<thought>We need to determine the number of carbonyl groups in the unknown molecule. The most direct way is to retrieve its 13C NMR spectrum and count the signals that fall in the typical carbonyl carbon chemical shift range (≈190–220 ppm). This will give us the number of distinct carbonyl carbons, which equals the number of carbonyl groups. We'll request the carbon NMR data using the provided tool.</thought>
